newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - most up but CFDs still slip lower.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - most up but CFDs still slip lower.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly slightly firmer on Thursday although Brent crude CFDs, which fell sharply on Wednesday, were slightly easier.
Heavy fuel rose $1.50 a tonne towards $86.50 for May and June amid support from Singapore and some local bunker demand.
Further forward the contango between the third and fourth quarters firmed to $6 a tonne at $87.50 and $93.50 respectively.
Low sulphur remained only $5.50 a tonne above barges on the front end which is low historically but reflects poor demand from Italy in recent months.
Gasoline rose 50 cents to $204.50 for June but activity was limited to a barge trade at $203.50.
July remained some $4.50 below June with August a further $3.50 lower.
Naphtha rose $2 a tonne to $188.50 for June and July with the third and fourth quarter cracks holding steady around $1.95 a barrel.
Brent CFDs slipped eight cents a barrel to 24 cents under July for next week and 23 cents under, 19 cents and 20 cents under for the three subsequent weeks.
A 1-30 June CFD traded ar 21 cents under July.
Jet premiums were little changed, with June and July at $20 a tonne and $21 a tonne above the IPE rspectively.
Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.75 (1Q98). -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
